sn18.1:1.3: Rāhula was the Buddha’s son to his wife Bhaddakaccānā ([an1.245]()). Rāhula’s going forth is related at [pli-tv-kd1:54.1.1](), and other important discourses with him include [mn61](), [mn62](), and [mn147]() = [sn35.121](). In the latter he became an arahant, which he confirmed in his own words at [thag4.8](). Commentaries explain his name as meaning “bondage”, but it probably refers rather to being born under the influence of the dark star Rāhu ([sn2.8]()). The Buddha declared him the foremost of monks who desire training ([an1.209]()). This is illustrated in this series of lessons through which Rāhula doggedly persists. His death is not noted in the early texts.
sn18.1:4.1: In this and similar passages, Mahāsaṅgīti edition inserts unnecessary ellipses.
